For a list of the bare minimum stuff you would need to have to do your own home repairs and routine maintenance, see [part 1](https://voat.co/v/Bicycling/comments/1114175). Part 2 covers stuff that's good to have on hand, but you may not necessarily need or want to keep it around if you don't plan on doing very much maintenance.

* Diagonal Wire Cutters (they're often better for cutting brake housing than a dedicated set of bike cable and housing cutters) * File * Chain Wear Checker * Magnetic Tray * Work Stand (expensive, but you can make your own if you're on a tight budget; check youtube for DIY ideas) * Spare brake and shifter cables * Spare brake and shifter cable housing (brake housing and shifter housing are different, do not mix them up!) * Cable End Crimps * Spare Ferrules, both types * Cheater Bar (an ordinary section of pipe that fits over the end of a wrench to give you additional leverage for removing extremely tight parts) * Toolbox (duh) * Rubber Mallet * Dedicated Storage for for Spare Parts (you **will** accumulate these and you **will** use many of them eventually, especially screws, nuts, and washers) * Ziplock Bags * Disposable Gloves * Electrical Tape * Scissors * Old Inner Tubes * Zip Ties * Ratchet Set * Full Set of Metric Box Wrenches (ratcheting are best, but are more expensive) * Digital Calipers * Hacksaw (tons of uses for this, one being the removal of stripped screws by cutting through them or making a slit in the head to insert a screwdriver) * Measuring tape w/metric and imperial * String * Torque Wrench * Shop Rags * White or Metallic Pen * Super Glue * Acetone (Nail Polish Remover) * 70-90% Isopropyl Alcohol (a.k.a Rubbing Alcohol) * Bucket * Sponge * Degreaser * Rust Remover (vinegar often works in a pinch) * Vice * Trash Can! * Laptop with Internet (Don't run to your desk every time you need to look something up or put on some entertainment while you work! Use a laptop!) * Drinks and Snacks
Tools for home bike repairs, part 2

• Pipe cutter (useful to cut seat posts, head tubes, and handlebars)
  • Master link tool
  • Vice Grips
  • Headset Wrench
  • A straight edge (like a level)
  • Digital scale (for weighing individual parts)
  • Digital luggage scale (for weighing the complete bike)
